customers.title: Electric and gas customers
customers.content:
Metered electric and gas customer counts across both utility subsidiaries.

For Alliant Energy Corporation: IPL (Iowa) and WPL (Wisconsin) grow customers at roughly 1% a year, which is a small part of the earnings story; the bigger lever is the rate base below, and the authorized ROE it's allowed to earn.

What to watch:

  • Customer growth tracking local population/economic growth, not a cyclical swing
  • Electric growth outpacing gas (electrification of heating and EVs)

rateBase.title: Rate base by segment
rateBase.content:
Rate base is the capital regulators allow each utility to earn a return on -- the core driver of a regulated utility's earnings growth, since EPS grows roughly with (rate base × authorized ROE) net of financing cost.

For Alliant Energy Corporation: IPL's retail electric rate base ($7.3bn) is the single largest segment, with WPL retail electric ($6.2bn) close behind; wholesale and gas are small by comparison. Only FY2025 is disclosed in filings to date, so this chart will build a trend as later 10-Ks report it.

What to watch:

  • Rate base growing in line with the disclosed CapEx plan
  • Regulatory lag -- rate cases that recover the capital at the authorized ROE, not a discount to it

salesMix.title: Electric sales volume by customer class
salesMix.content:
Retail electric sales volume (GWh) split between residential, commercial and industrial customers.

For Alliant Energy Corporation: industrial load (data centers, ag processing) is the largest and most volatile class; residential volume is weather-driven (heating/cooling degree days) and shows up as noise rather than a trend in a single FY figure.

What to watch:

  • Industrial volume growth -- new large-load interconnections (e.g. data centers) are the upside case for rate-base growth
  • Residential volume flat to declining on efficiency gains, offset by electrification

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Alliant Energy Corporation: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Alliant Energy Corporation: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Alliant Energy Corporation: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Alliant Energy Corporation: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Alliant Energy Corporation: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Alliant Energy Corporation: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Alliant Energy Corporation: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Alliant Energy Corporation: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Alliant Energy Corporation: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Alliant Energy Corporation: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
